sources.title: National flood risk standing advice for local planning authorities
sources.role: EA standing advice for planning authorities
sources.facts: Updated 28 May 2026; directs LPAs on site research, FRAs, SuDS, tests and when to consult the EA or LLFA.
sources.guard: Standing advice is a review route, not an approval, permit or parcel-safe conclusion.

sources.title: Flood risk assessments: applying for planning permission
sources.facts: Updated 28 May 2026; explains when FRAs and drainage strategies are needed and warns about limitations of existing models.
sources.guard: Preparing an FRA does not establish acceptability, model fitness, consent or absence of residual risk.

sources.title: Flood risk and coastal change
sources.facts: Explains flood zones, sequential and exception tests, development lifetime and coastal change policy.
sources.guard: Policy categorisation does not replace site-specific evidence, current mapping, drainage design or decision-making.

sources.title: National standards for sustainable drainage systems
sources.facts: Published 19 June 2025; covers design, maintenance and operation of surface-water drainage systems in England.
sources.guard: Conformance claims require project evidence; standards alone do not prove capacity, maintenance funding or approval.

sources.title: Flood risk assessments: climate change allowances
sources.facts: Provides allowances for future flood risk assessment and points to planning guidance on flood risk and coastal change.
sources.guard: An allowance is a scenario input, not an observed event, probability guarantee or exact property forecast.

sources.title: How to prepare a strategic flood risk assessment
sources.facts: Requires appraisal of dataset suitability, new and emerging flood data and expected climate effects.
sources.guard: An SFRA is strategic evidence and cannot substitute for parcel-level FRA, current survey or planning decision.

sources.title: Reservoir flood maps: when and how to use them
sources.facts: Explains appropriate use of reservoir flood mapping for plan and emergency planning contexts.
sources.guard: Reservoir mapping is scenario evidence, not a prediction of failure, property damage or insurance outcome.

sources.title: Using modelling for flood risk assessments
sources.facts: Guidance for applicants, developers and consultants on using modelling in FRAs for planning permission.
sources.guard: A model result depends on inputs, calibration and scope; it is not an observed event or automatic acceptance.
